course.title: Home Workout and Bodyweight
course.tagline: Get strong at home with no gym: push-ups, squats and full routines.

days.title: Your first home workout
days.goal: Do a short, easy full-body workout at home with no tools.

video.title: 10 MIN FULL BODY WORKOUT 🔥 For Beginners | No Equipment

steps: Clear a small space on the floor, about the size of a mat.
Watch the video and follow the warm-up moves.
Do the workout at your own pace and rest when you need to.
Drink water and write down how you felt after.
days.task: Finish the 10-minute workout and write how you felt.
days.challenge: Do the workout again tomorrow and try one more rep of each move.

quiz.q: What do you need for a home workout?
options: A small clear space and your body
quiz.explain: Your body and a little space are enough to start.

quiz.q: What should you do if a move feels too hard?
options: Slow down or rest, then try an easier version
quiz.explain: Slowing down or using an easier version keeps you safe.

quiz.q: Why drink water during a workout?
options: Water replaces what you lose in sweat
quiz.explain: Drinking water keeps you cool and strong.

days.title: Warm up before you move
days.goal: Learn a simple warm-up that wakes up your body.
steps: March in place for 1 minute.
Roll your shoulders back 10 times, then forward 10 times.
Swing each leg gently forward and back 5 times.
Reach your arms up high and breathe in, then relax.
days.task: Do this warm-up before every workout this week.
days.challenge: Teach the warm-up to a family member from memory.

quiz.q: Why warm up first?
options: It gets blood moving and helps you avoid injury
quiz.explain: A warm-up wakes up muscles so they move safely.

quiz.q: How long should a warm-up take?
quiz.explain: Five minutes is enough to get the body ready.

quiz.q: What is a good warm-up move?
quiz.explain: Marching is gentle and raises your heart rate a little.

days.title: Learn the squat
days.goal: Learn a safe bodyweight squat you can do at home.
steps: Stand with feet a little wider than your hips.
Push your hips back like you are sitting in a chair.
Keep your chest up and your knees pointing with your toes.
Stand back up and press through your whole foot.
days.task: Do 3 sets of 8 slow squats.
days.challenge: Do 10 squats with a 3-second slow way down.

quiz.q: Where should your knees point in a squat?
options: The same way as your toes
quiz.explain: Knees following the toes keeps the knee safe.

quiz.q: What should your chest do?
quiz.explain: A tall chest keeps your back safe.

quiz.q: How do you stand back up?
quiz.explain: Pressing through the foot gives a strong, steady stand.

days.title: Learn the push-up
days.goal: Learn a push-up and the easy versions that build strength.
steps: Start with a wall push-up: hands on a wall, body straight.
Bend your elbows and bring your chest to the wall, then push back.
Try a knee push-up on the floor with a straight body.
Keep your belly tight so your hips do not sag.
days.task: Do 3 sets of 5 wall push-ups.
days.challenge: Try one knee push-up on the floor with good form.

quiz.q: What should your body look like in a push-up?
options: One straight line from head to knees or toes
quiz.explain: A straight line keeps your back safe.

quiz.q: What is a good first push-up?
options: A push-up with a bag on your back
quiz.explain: A wall push-up is easy and safe to learn.

quiz.q: Where do your hands go?
quiz.explain: Hands under the shoulders give a strong push.

days.title: Train your legs at home
days.goal: Build leg strength with squats and lunges.

video.title: How to Do a Proper Push-Up

steps: Do 10 squats, slow and steady.
Try a lunge: step forward, bend both knees, then step back.
Do 6 lunges on each leg.
Rest 1 minute, then repeat the round once more.
days.task: Do 2 rounds of 10 squats and 6 lunges per leg.
days.challenge: Hold the bottom of a squat for 5 seconds, 3 times.

quiz.q: What is a lunge?
options: A step forward with both knees bent
quiz.explain: A lunge steps forward and bends both knees.

quiz.q: What muscles do squats and lunges work?
quiz.explain: Squats and lunges build the legs and glutes.

quiz.q: How long should you rest between rounds?
quiz.explain: A minute of rest lets you catch your breath.

days.title: Train your core at home
days.goal: Learn a simple plank and other core moves.

video.title: How to Do a Proper Bodyweight Squat

steps: Learn the plank: forearms on the floor, body straight, hold 10 seconds.
Try a dead bug: lie on your back, arms up, knees up, lower one arm and the other leg.
Do a glute bridge: lie down, knees bent, lift your hips up.
Breathe normally during each move.
days.task: Hold a plank for 20 seconds, 3 times.
days.challenge: Do 10 glute bridges with a 2-second hold at the top.

quiz.q: What is your core?
options: The muscles around your belly and lower back
quiz.explain: Core muscles hold your body steady.

quiz.q: What should your body look like in a plank?
options: One straight line from head to heels
quiz.explain: A straight line keeps the plank safe and useful.

quiz.q: Why breathe during a plank?
options: Breathing keeps you calm and steady
quiz.explain: Steady breathing stops dizziness and keeps you strong.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Your first full-body routine
days.goal: Put week 1 together: build your own full-body routine.

video.title: 15-Minute Beginner Full Body Workout | No Equipment, No Jumping

steps: Pick one move for legs, one for pushing, one for the middle.
Write your routine: 2 sets of 8 to 10 reps of each move.
Add your warm-up at the start.
Do the whole routine and write how it felt.
days.task: Do your full routine and record your reps.
days.challenge: Do the routine without looking at your notes.

quiz.q: What should a full-body routine have?
options: Moves for legs, pushing and core
quiz.explain: A full-body routine works the whole body.

quiz.q: How many sets suit a beginner?
quiz.explain: Two sets is enough to learn and get stronger.

quiz.q: What should you add at the start?
quiz.explain: A warm-up gets the body ready.

project.title: Your first full-body routine
project.brief: Build your own full-body routine with 3 moves, a warm-up, and 2 sets of each move, then do it and record your reps.
checks: Routine has leg, push and core moves
Routine has 2 sets of each move

days.title: Rest and stretch day
days.goal: Learn why rest days help and how to stretch gently.

video.title: Total Body Strength Training Without Weights for Women

steps: Take a slow walk for 10 minutes.
Stretch your legs: hold each stretch for 20 seconds.
Stretch your arms and chest gently.
Write down how your body feels today.
days.task: Take a 10-minute walk and stretch for 5 minutes.
days.challenge: Hold each stretch for 30 seconds instead of 20.

quiz.q: Why take a rest day?
options: Muscles repair and grow stronger on rest days
quiz.explain: Rest is when the body repairs and gets stronger.

quiz.q: How long should you hold a gentle stretch?
quiz.explain: Twenty seconds lets the muscle relax.

quiz.q: What is a good rest-day activity?
quiz.explain: A slow walk keeps you moving without strain.

days.title: Push-ups: get stronger step by step
days.goal: Move from wall push-ups to knee push-ups.
steps: Do 10 wall push-ups with a straight body.
Try 5 knee push-ups on the floor.
Rest 1 minute between sets.
Write down how many you did with good form.
days.task: Do 3 sets of 5 knee push-ups.
days.challenge: Try one full push-up from your toes.

quiz.q: What comes after wall push-ups?
quiz.explain: Knee push-ups are the next easy step.

quiz.q: Why keep good form?
options: Good form keeps you safe and works the right muscles
quiz.explain: Good form protects you and builds real strength.

quiz.q: What should you do if your hips sag?
options: Rest and try again with fewer reps
quiz.explain: Resting and doing fewer reps keeps form safe.

days.title: Squats: go a little deeper
days.goal: Make your squat stronger by going a little lower.
steps: Do 10 squats to a chair: sit down lightly, then stand up.
Try 10 squats without the chair.
Keep your heels on the floor the whole time.
Write down how deep you could go with good form.
days.task: Do 3 sets of 10 chair squats.
days.challenge: Hold a squat at the bottom for 3 seconds, 5 times.

quiz.q: Why use a chair for squats?
options: It is only for old people
It helps you learn depth safely
quiz.explain: A chair gives you a safe target to sit toward.

quiz.q: What should your heels do in a squat?
quiz.explain: Heels on the floor keep you balanced and safe.

quiz.q: How deep should a beginner squat?
options: As deep as you can with good form
As deep as possible no matter what
quiz.explain: Depth with good form is the safe goal.

days.title: Add a little cardio at home
days.goal: Raise your heart rate with easy moves and no jumping.
steps: March in place for 1 minute.
Do step touches side to side for 1 minute.
Do slow knee lifts for 1 minute.
Rest and check your breathing: you should be able to talk.
days.task: Do 3 rounds of 1 minute marching, 1 minute step touches.
days.challenge: Add arm swings to your marching.

quiz.q: What is cardio?
options: Exercise that makes your heart beat faster
quiz.explain: Cardio trains your heart and lungs.

quiz.q: How should you feel during easy cardio?
options: Warm and breathing faster, but still able to talk
quiz.explain: You should be warm but still able to talk.

quiz.q: What is a good no-jump cardio move?
quiz.explain: Marching raises the heart rate without impact.

days.title: Build a 20-minute workout
days.goal: Put your moves into a 20-minute routine.
steps: Warm up for 5 minutes.
Do 3 rounds: 10 squats, 5 push-ups, 10 glute bridges, 20-second plank.
Rest 1 minute between rounds.
Cool down with slow walking and stretching.
days.task: Finish the 20-minute workout and record your numbers.
days.challenge: Add 2 reps to each move next time.

quiz.q: How long should a beginner workout be?
quiz.explain: Twenty minutes is enough to train and recover.

quiz.q: What should you do between rounds?
quiz.explain: A short rest lets you keep good form.

quiz.q: What should you do at the end?
options: Cool down with slow walking and stretching
Eat a big meal at once
quiz.explain: A cool-down helps the body slow down gently.

days.title: Learn the lunge well
days.goal: Practise lunges with balance and good form.

video.title: 20-Min Low Impact Cardio Workout | No Jumping, No Equipment

steps: Stand tall and step forward with one foot.
Bend both knees until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push back to standing through your front foot.
Hold a chair for balance if you need it.
days.task: Do 3 sets of 6 lunges per leg.
days.challenge: Do lunges without holding anything.

quiz.q: What should your front knee do in a lunge?
options: Point the same way as your toes
quiz.explain: The knee should follow the toes for safety.

quiz.q: What can you hold for balance?
quiz.explain: A chair helps you stay steady while you learn.

quiz.q: How do you come back up from a lunge?
quiz.explain: Pushing through the front foot brings you up strong.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Your 20-minute routine
days.goal: Put week 2 together: write and test your own 20-minute routine.

video.title: Beginner Workout at Home for Women Day 1

steps: Write your routine: warm-up, 4 moves, cool-down.
Do the routine and time each part.
Write down your reps for each move.
Change one thing to make it a little harder next week.
days.task: Write your routine and do it from start to finish.
days.challenge: Do the routine in under 20 minutes.

quiz.q: What should your routine include?
quiz.explain: A full routine warms up, works and cools down.

quiz.q: Why write down your reps?
options: So you can see progress next week
quiz.explain: Written reps show you getting stronger.

quiz.q: How do you make next week harder?
options: Add a few reps or one more round
quiz.explain: Small adds keep progress safe.

project.title: Your 20-minute routine
project.brief: Write and test your own 20-minute routine with 4 moves, a warm-up and a cool-down, and record your numbers.
checks: Routine has a warm-up and cool-down
Named one way to make it harder

days.title: Try a gentle HIIT round
days.goal: Learn what HIIT is and try a slow, easy version.
steps: HIIT means short bursts of work with rest in between.
Work for 20 seconds, rest for 40 seconds.
Try: march fast, squats, step touches, knee lifts.
Do 4 rounds and rest well between them.
days.task: Do 4 rounds of 20 seconds work, 40 seconds rest.
days.challenge: Try 30 seconds work, 30 seconds rest.

quiz.q: What does HIIT mean?
options: Short bursts of work with rest in between
quiz.explain: HIIT mixes short hard work with rest.

quiz.q: How long should a beginner work in HIIT?
quiz.explain: Short work with long rest suits a beginner.

quiz.q: What should you do if you feel dizzy?
options: Stop, sit down and drink water
quiz.explain: Stopping when dizzy keeps you safe.

days.title: Train your back at home
days.goal: Learn simple moves for your back with no tools.

video.title: 10 MIN FULL BODY WORKOUT 🔥 For Beginners | No Equipment

steps: Try a superman: lie face down, lift arms and legs a little.
Try a table row: hold a sturdy table edge and pull your chest up.
Do a slow bird dog: on hands and knees, stretch one arm and the other leg.
Keep your back flat and breathe normally.
days.task: Do 2 sets of 8 supermans and 8 bird dogs per side.
days.challenge: Hold each superman for 3 seconds.

quiz.q: What does a superman work?
quiz.explain: A superman trains the back of the body.

quiz.q: What is a bird dog?
options: On hands and knees, stretch one arm and the other leg
quiz.explain: A bird dog trains balance and the core.

quiz.q: Why train your back?
options: A strong back helps you stand tall and avoid pain
quiz.explain: Back strength supports good posture.

days.title: Train your arms at home
days.goal: Build arm strength with push-ups and chair dips.
steps: Do 5 wall push-ups.
Try a chair dip: hands on a chair behind you, bend your elbows.
Do 5 chair dips slowly.
Rest 1 minute and repeat once.
days.task: Do 2 sets of 5 push-ups and 5 chair dips.
days.challenge: Try a knee push-up instead of a wall push-up.

quiz.q: What is a chair dip?
options: Hands on a chair, bend elbows to lower the body
quiz.explain: A chair dip trains the back of the arms.

quiz.q: What should you check in a chair dip?
options: That the chair is sturdy and will not move
quiz.explain: A sturdy chair keeps you safe.

quiz.q: What do push-ups train?
quiz.explain: Push-ups train the pushing muscles.

days.title: Make a weekly plan
days.goal: Plan your workouts for the whole week.
steps: Pick 3 days to train and 4 days to rest or walk.
Write which moves you will do each day.
Put the plan where you can see it.
Tick off each workout when you finish it.
days.task: Write your weekly plan and stick it on a wall.
days.challenge: Tick off all 3 workouts this week.

quiz.q: How many training days suit a beginner?
quiz.explain: Three days gives growth and rest.

quiz.q: Why write your plan down?
options: So you can see it and stay on track
quiz.explain: A written plan is easy to follow.

quiz.q: What should you do on rest days?
quiz.explain: Gentle movement on rest days helps recovery.

days.title: Test yourself: how far have you come?
days.goal: Test your strength with simple counts.
steps: Count how many squats you can do in 1 minute.
Count how many push-ups you can do with good form.
Time how long you can hold a plank.
Write all three numbers down.
days.task: Record your 3 test numbers today.
days.challenge: Beat one of your numbers by next week.

quiz.q: Why test yourself?
options: To see how much stronger you have become
quiz.explain: Tests show your progress in numbers.

quiz.q: What should you do if a number is lower?
options: Keep training and test again in 2 weeks
Train twice as hard at once
quiz.explain: Numbers go up and down; steady training brings them up.

quiz.q: How often should you test?
quiz.explain: A few weeks apart shows real change.

days.title: Try a longer workout
days.goal: Do a 30-minute workout with more rounds.

video.title: How to Do a Proper Push-Up

steps: Warm up for 5 minutes.
Do 4 rounds: 10 squats, 8 push-ups, 10 lunges, 10 glute bridges, 20-second plank.
Rest 1 minute between rounds.
Cool down for 5 minutes.
days.task: Finish the 30-minute workout.
days.challenge: Add one more round next time.

quiz.q: How do you make a workout longer safely?
options: Go as fast as you can
quiz.explain: One more round is a safe small step.

quiz.q: What should you do if you get very tired?
quiz.explain: Resting longer keeps form safe.

quiz.q: What is a cool-down?
options: Slow moves that help the body calm down
quiz.explain: A cool-down slows the heart rate gently.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Your 30-minute routine
days.goal: Put week 3 together: build and test your own 30-minute routine.

video.title: How to Do a Proper Bodyweight Squat

steps: Write a 30-minute routine with 5 moves.
Do the routine and time it.
Write down your reps and how you felt.
Fix anything that felt too hard or too easy.
days.task: Write and complete your 30-minute routine.
days.challenge: Do the routine twice this week.

quiz.q: What should a 30-minute routine have?
quiz.explain: A full routine warms up, works and cools down.

quiz.q: How do you know if a move is too hard?
quiz.explain: Losing form means the move is too hard right now.

quiz.q: What should you fix after testing?
options: Anything too hard or too easy
quiz.explain: Small fixes make the routine fit you better.

project.title: Your 30-minute routine
project.brief: Build and test your own 30-minute routine with 5 moves, good form and steady breathing.
checks: Routine has a warm-up and cool-down
Kept good form the whole time

days.title: Balance and control
days.goal: Practise standing on one leg and moving with control.

video.title: 15-Minute Beginner Full Body Workout | No Equipment, No Jumping

steps: Stand on one leg for 20 seconds, then switch.
Try a slow step-up on a low step.
Do 5 slow step-ups per leg.
Keep your eyes forward and breathe normally.
days.task: Stand on each leg for 30 seconds.
days.challenge: Do step-ups without holding anything.

quiz.q: Why train balance?
options: Balance stops falls and helps every move
quiz.explain: Good balance keeps you steady and safe.

quiz.q: What is a step-up?
options: Stepping up onto a low step and back down
quiz.explain: A step-up trains legs and balance.

quiz.q: What should your eyes do during balance work?
quiz.explain: Looking at one spot helps you stay steady.

days.title: Full-body circuit day
days.goal: Do a circuit: move from one exercise to the next with short rests.

video.title: Total Body Strength Training Without Weights for Women

steps: A circuit means doing moves one after another.
Do: 10 squats, 8 push-ups, 10 lunges, 10 bridges, 20-second plank.
Rest 1 minute, then repeat 3 times.
Write down your total time.
days.task: Complete 3 rounds of the circuit.
days.challenge: Beat your total time by 1 minute next time.

quiz.q: What is a circuit?
options: Moves done one after another with short rests
quiz.explain: A circuit links moves together in a round.

quiz.q: How long should you rest between rounds?
quiz.explain: A minute of rest keeps the circuit safe.

quiz.q: Why write down your time?
options: So you can see yourself getting faster and fitter
quiz.explain: Your time shows progress.

days.title: Fix common mistakes
days.goal: Learn the 3 most common home-workout mistakes and how to fix them.
steps: Mistake 1: rushing. Fix: move slowly and count to 3.
Mistake 2: holding your breath. Fix: breathe out on the hard part.
Mistake 3: skipping the warm-up. Fix: always warm up 5 minutes.
Pick one mistake you make and fix it today.
days.task: Pick one mistake and fix it in today's workout.
days.challenge: Teach a friend the 3 mistakes and their fixes.

quiz.q: Why is rushing a mistake?
options: Rushing breaks your form and can hurt you
quiz.explain: Slow, controlled moves are safer and work better.

quiz.q: When should you breathe out?
options: On the hard part of the move
quiz.explain: Breathing out on the hard part keeps you steady.

quiz.q: Why never skip the warm-up?
options: It gets the body ready and lowers injury risk
quiz.explain: A warm-up prepares muscles and joints.

days.title: Train with a friend
days.goal: Work out with a friend and help each other.
steps: Invite a friend to do your routine with you.
Take turns watching each other's form.
Cheer each other on after each round.
Write down what your friend did well.
days.task: Do a workout with a friend this week.
days.challenge: Teach your friend your favourite move.

quiz.q: Why train with a friend?
options: Friends keep you going and make it fun
quiz.explain: A friend adds fun and keeps you honest.

quiz.q: What should you watch in a friend's form?
quiz.explain: Watching form helps your friend stay safe.

quiz.q: What should you say after a round?
options: Kind words about what went well
quiz.explain: Kind words keep a friend coming back.

days.title: Make your routine harder, the safe way
days.goal: Learn 3 safe ways to make moves harder.
steps: Add reps: do 12 instead of 10.
Slow down: take 3 seconds to lower down.
Add a hold: pause for 2 seconds at the hard part.
Pick one way and use it this week.
days.task: Pick one way to make your routine harder.
days.challenge: Try all 3 ways on different moves.

quiz.q: What is a safe way to make a move harder?
options: Add a few reps or slow down
quiz.explain: Small adds keep progress safe.

quiz.q: Why slow down a move?
options: Slow moves work the muscle more and keep form safe
quiz.explain: Slow, controlled moves build strength safely.

quiz.q: What is a hold?
options: Pausing still at the hard part of a move
quiz.explain: A hold makes the muscle work without moving.

days.title: Stretch and move well
days.goal: Learn a 10-minute stretch routine for the whole body.
steps: Stretch your legs, hips, chest and shoulders.
Hold each stretch for 20 to 30 seconds.
Breathe slowly and never bounce.
Write down which stretch felt best.
days.task: Do the 10-minute stretch routine.
days.challenge: Hold each stretch for 30 seconds.

quiz.q: Why stretch after a workout?
options: It makes you stronger at once
It helps muscles relax and feel less stiff
quiz.explain: Stretching after a workout eases stiffness.

quiz.q: Why not bounce in a stretch?
quiz.explain: Slow, still stretches are safe.

quiz.q: How should you breathe while stretching?
quiz.explain: Slow breathing helps the muscle relax.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final routine.

video.title: 20-Min Low Impact Cardio Workout | No Jumping, No Equipment

steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 moves you can now do well.
Practise your capstone routine once.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 moves you can do well now.
days.challenge: Do your capstone routine from memory.

quiz.q: What is the capstone?
options: A final project that shows what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can do a full routine safely from memory
quiz.explain: Doing a full routine well shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone routine once more, then rest.

video.title: Beginner Workout at Home for Women Day 1

steps: Do your capstone routine one more time.
Time each part and check your form.
Fix anything that felt rushed.
Rest well tonight and drink water.
days.task: Run your capstone routine and time each part.
days.challenge: Fix one thing that felt rushed.

quiz.q: Why practise once more?
options: Practice makes the real run calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
options: Your form, your timing and your breathing
quiz.explain: Checking form, timing and breathing makes the routine smooth.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you perform your best.

days.title: Capstone day: your 30-minute routine
days.goal: Show what you learned: do your full 30-minute routine with good form.
steps: Warm up for 5 minutes.
Do your full routine: 5 moves, good form, steady breathing.
Cool down and stretch for 5 minutes.
Write a short report: what you did and how it felt.
days.task: Complete your capstone routine and write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: What is the first step of your capstone?
quiz.explain: A warm-up gets the body ready and safe.

quiz.q: What matters most in the capstone?
options: Going as fast as you can
quiz.explain: Good form and breathing show real skill.

quiz.q: What goes in your report?
options: What you did and how it felt
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Your 30-minute home routine
capstone.brief: Perform your own 30-minute full-body home routine from start to finish: warm-up, 5 moves with good form, cool-down, and a short written report.
checks: Did all 5 moves with good form
deliverables: A list of your test numbers
A short video or notes from the routine
